evidence.text: The entry analyzes 錯 as 从金、昔聲 and gives the original meaning as a whetstone used to work jade or stone. It cites 尚書《禹貢》「錫貢磬錯」 with Kong Anguo’s explanation that 錯 is used to work jade/stone. It separately records metal inlay/decorating in 《鹽鐵論》 and 《國語》, file/tool use in 《列女傳》, polishing in 《鶡冠子》, intercrossing in 《詩經》, mixed/disordered use in 《尚書》, alternating in Wang Bo’s Tang verse, and wrong/error in 《墨子》. These are examples attributed to named works; they do not establish a secure continuous semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：錯

evidence.text: The page displays a small-seal image, one bamboo/silk example, and later forms, but no oracle-bone or bronze forms for 錯. Its text supports a 金 semantic component and 昔 phonetic component. No specific loss or corruption of 昔 is described. The page’s linked image files were attempted but could not be fetched by the browser; exact stroke transitions are therefore unverified.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：錯

evidence.text: The entry records 倉故切 as a departing-tone reading in 模/暮 and 倉各切 as an entering-tone reading in 唐/鐸. Both should be kept distinct. Its listed modern Mandarin reading is cuò; the presence of multiple historical readings cautions against assuming every sense shared one pronunciation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：錯

evidence.text: CUHK analyzes 昔 in early forms as 日 plus 𡿧, which it interprets as an early 災 form, and proposes an original flood/disaster interpretation extended to ‘formerly’. It cites oracle-bone 《合集》137反 and 301 for ‘formerly’, a bronze inscription on 曶鼎 for a past famine year, and Warring States bamboo slips for ‘formerly’. The entry notes that Shuowen instead explains 昔 as dried meat; CUHK considers that account to concern 腊. This independent history of 昔 does not make its meaning part of 錯.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析「昔」

evidence.text: For 錯, Dong Chinese labels 釒 as the meaning component and 昔 as the sound component, giving Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms 錯 *[tsʰ]ˤak and 昔 *[s]Ak. In its displayed historical table, 錯 is Middle Chinese tshak and modern Mandarin cuò; 昔 is Middle Chinese sjek and modern Mandarin xī. These are character-level reconstructions/readings, not independent proof of a single continuous sound history across every sense.
evidence.title: 錯 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.text: The 錯 page labels its seal example as Shuowen, approximately 100 CE, and its clerical example as Eastern Han, 25–220 CE. The image links refer to hosted paleographic images but failed to load through the web tool. The source calls 昔 phonetic and supplies Old Chinese comparisons; its assertion is compatible with the Shuowen analysis, while the image page descriptions alone do not establish detailed graphic changes.
evidence.title: 錯 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.text: A 2015 Baxter–Sagart draft groups 昔 (MC sjek, OC *[s]Ak) and 錯 (MC tshak, OC *[tsʰ]ˤak) in its GSR 798 discussion, alongside related readings. This gives same-system historical comparisons for the phonetic component and 錯. These are reconstructions, not directly attested pronunciations. The accessible draft does not by itself demonstrate that all senses of 錯 were pronounced alike.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart 11/09/15 draft

evidence.text: The dictionary cites 《詩經·小雅·鶴鳴》「它山之石，可以為錯」 with Mao’s gloss that 錯 is stone usable for working jade; it also lists intercrossing in 《詩經·楚茨》 and metal decoration in 《國語》. Its reproduction of Kangxi and Shuowen materials distinguishes these gloss traditions: Kangxi records whetstone, inlay, mixed/disordered, alternating, and wrong/error senses, while the reproduced Shuowen says 金涂也 and 从金昔聲. The source list does not date textual witnesses individually, so it cannot alone yield a chronology.
evidence.title: 錯 cuò、cù、xī - 汉典

evidence.source: 漢典 ZDIC reproducing Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.text: Duan Yucai’s later commentary distinguishes 錯 borrowed for 措 ‘place’, for 厝 ‘whetstone’, and for 交錯 ‘crossing/interlacing’. This is a later philological account and does not directly establish the chronological order of the meanings. It concerns graph borrowing among words, which is distinct from 昔 serving as a phonetic element within 錯.
evidence.title: 錯 cuò、cù、xī - 汉典

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education)
evidence.text: The entry describes 䥘 as a variant treated as a regular-script adaptation of the seal form. It also records 厝 as a variant reading/graph associated with 錯 in the whetstone passage, citing Duan Yucai. This documents variant and borrowing traditions; it is not evidence that 厂 was a component in the ancestry of 錯.
evidence.title: A04310 錯 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: Search results identify a seal-script (說文小篆) entry for 錯 and describe the form as 䥘. The dictionary page could not be opened during this research, so this result was not used to establish details beyond the existence of a possible seal-form candidate.
evidence.title: 錯 - Chinese Text Project

evidence.field: small seal script category and reuse context
evidence.text: The category describes small seal script as a Chinese script form standardized and promulgated by the Qin dynasty and lists sample media. It provides a route to individual file descriptions, but the searched material did not yield a character-specific 錯 glyph file with verified reuse provenance.

gaps: The dossier note that 昔 was once present in a gold component and then lost is unsupported by the inspected external sources; no source describes the loss or corruption of 昔 in 錯.

The oldest forms of 錯 identified in the inspected sources are a Shuowen seal form and a Qin/Han manuscript tradition, not oracle-bone or bronze attestations. Linked CUHK and Dong image assets were inaccessible through the browser.
No independent early graphic history for the 金 element as used in 錯 was established. The semantic role is supported by the traditional 金涂 gloss and modern dictionary analysis.

The sound role of 昔 is independently asserted in Shuowen and modern analyses. Same-system Baxter–Sagart comparisons are available for 昔 *[s]Ak and 錯 *[tsʰ]ˤak (with Middle Chinese sjek and tshak), but reconstructions remain hypotheses and do not establish a sound match for every sense.

The sense attestations are cited to different works, but their witness dates and links among whetstone, polishing, intercrossing/mixing, and wrong/error are not fully established. The gloss lists do not determine a chronology.
The whole-graph borrowing explanation for 措/厝/交錯 is a later philological claim. No proposed loan here depends on identifying the name of a depicted tool or object.
The simplified relation 错 ← 錯 is listed by dictionaries; the specific adoption date and standardization pathway were not established from a primary source.

No character-specific image with both usable direct-image identity and verified reuse license/provenance was established after searching Commons and source pages. Commons candidates were either unrelated or general samples; therefore no glyph image is proposed. The CUHK/Dong actual 錯 image assets could not be fetched for license or pixel review.

limitations.text: Searches of Commons for 錯/错 seal and small-seal script did not yield an exact character glyph file with rights information. CUHK and Dong pages identify seal-script or manuscript examples, but linked direct image assets failed to load. No image is proposed because identity and reuse provenance could not both be established; the pages also do not supply a usable license for their glyph assets.
